These primitives form the basis for constructing Bayesian belief networks in GSI where each tournament's level reflects its relative importance or frequency of occurrence. The sport_slug provides a semantic layer that allows GSE to route events into appropriate processing pipelines. The interplay between these fields enables dualistic reasoning: one can infer both the structural position of a tournament (via level) and its domain (via sport_slug), which together define a conditional probability space. Failure modes include missing or malformed slugs leading to indexing errors, and undefined levels causing misclassification in hierarchical models. This structure supports retroactive analysis of historical performance trends and enables real-time adaptation in dynamic environments.
